title: Unit sphere STL to Gmsh 3D tetrahedral volume mesh
overview:
QUICK COMMAND — closed STL to a 3-D TETRA_4 volume mesh:
python grid/stl_to_gmsh/generate_volume_mesh.py --stl path/to/sphere.stl --output $HOME/.oneflow/mesh-generation/sphere.msh --mesh-size 0.20

SIZE RANGE — allow Gmsh to choose between lower and upper target sizes:
python grid/stl_to_gmsh/generate_volume_mesh.py --stl path/to/sphere.stl --output $HOME/.oneflow/mesh-generation/sphere.msh --mesh-size-min 0.10 --mesh-size-max 0.20

One --mesh-size value sets both limits. Reuse the same STL and change only the size for coarse/medium/fine meshes. The command writes .msh, .geo and .report.json outputs. The native C++ and Python reference Cases remain available for the complete OneFLOW validation workflow.
principle: STL is a discrete triangle shell, not a CAD sphere and not a volume. A valid input for this Case must be one connected, closed, consistently oriented, non-degenerate genus-zero manifold shell. Gmsh ClassifySurfaces partitions the discrete facets into parametrizable patches; CreateGeometry reconstructs those patches; a Surface Loop and Volume define the enclosed fluid region. Physical Groups are dimension-tagged mesh semantics: wall is a dimension-2 exterior patch and fluid_domain is a dimension-3 volume. Neither name defines solver state data.
architecture: STL facets -> shell topology/orientation validation -> Gmsh merge and ClassifySurfaces -> parametrizable surface reconstruction -> one Surface Loop -> one Volume -> Physical Surface wall and Physical Volume fluid_domain -> first-order tetrahedral MSH 4.1. Native C++ runs through the OneFLOW Grid task and GridConversion; Python uses the shared STL surface utilities and converter as an independent reference. Both paths are registered as Cases and feed the shared Mesh-to-CFD Validation graph.

proves: The checked-in reference input is a closed, outward-oriented, connected unit-sphere STL shell with 1,280 triangular facets.
Native C++ and Python reference Cases consume byte-identical sphere STL inputs and share the same geometry and mesh-size contract.
The producer reconstructs one closed Gmsh surface loop and one volume and emits first-order tetrahedral MSH 4.1 with wall and fluid_domain Physical Groups.
The sphere mesh-size sweep varies target characteristic length at 0.40, 0.20 and 0.10 without asserting exact element counts.
The Mesh-to-CFD Workbench exposes the native and Python sphere Cases as a 3-D CFD smoke chain.
The direct STL volume mesh command exposes one-size and independent minimum/maximum characteristic-length controls and validates TETRA_4 volume output.
does_not_prove: The piecewise-planar STL is an exact analytic sphere or preserves exact CAD curvature.
The mesh-size parameter prescribes an exact number of nodes or tetrahedra.
The wall-only closed sphere setup represents external flow around a sphere.
A successful smoke run establishes CFD accuracy, convergence, conservation, grid independence or sphere aerodynamic coefficients.
Multiple shells, cavities, non-manifold surfaces, multi-volume assemblies, boundary-layer prisms or high-order tetrahedra are supported.

verification.scope: grid/tests/python/stl_to_gmsh/test_stl_to_gmsh_cases.py; checks paired native/Python registration, byte-identical input and unit-sphere layout contract.
tools/oneflow_gui/test_mesh_validation.py; checks both sphere Cases produce the four-stage STL-to-Gmsh, Gmsh-to-CGNS, CGNS-to-OneFLOW and 3-D CFD smoke graph.
grid/tests/python/stl_to_gmsh/test_stl_to_gmsh_geometry.py; executes the direct command against the reference sphere STL when Gmsh is available and checks TETRA_4/TRI_3 output and report.
